title: Conversion between square and cubic metric units
summary: Apply squared and cubed conversion factors to areas and volumes.
objectives: Distinguish linear, square and cubic conversion factors.
Convert reliably between cm² and m².
Convert reliably between cm³ and m³.

blocks.text: Apply squared and cubed conversion factors to areas and volumes. Keep every measurement in compatible units before substituting.
A linear conversion factor is applied once, a square-unit factor twice and a cubic-unit factor three times. Since 1 m=100 cm, 1 m²=100²=10,000 cm² and 1 m³=100³=1,000,000 cm³.

Write the conversion as a power before multiplying. Moving to a smaller unit increases the numerical value; moving to a larger unit decreases it. Convert all dimensions before using an area or volume formula, rather than converting the final result inconsistently.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: Convert 0.024 m³ to cm³ and then to litres.

sections.verification_note: 0.024 m³ is 24 dm³, and each dm³ is one litre.

blocks.text: Do not use the linear factor 100 for area or volume. Attach the exponent to the conversion factor. A quick direction check catches many errors: the number of square centimetres in one square metre must be much greater than one.
Sketch or decompose the figure, label compatible units, select the correct area or volume relationship, calculate in clear stages, and check that the final unit is squared or cubed as required.
Before moving on, explain the relevant property in words, show the equation or formula with units, and use the diagram markings to check that every correspondence is consistent.
